claims.text: Melting in FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles initiates through localized premelting at structural defect sites, particularly grain boundaries.
Accumulated energy and compositional fluctuations at defect sites lower the effective local melting threshold.
Local liquid zones propagate and coalesce to produce bulk nanoparticle melting.
The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles contain intrinsic grain boundaries and may contain slight compositional inhomogeneities.
A slow, stepwise heating ramp allows the nanoparticles to equilibrate at each temperature step.
An inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during heating.
A narrow nanoparticle size distribution minimizes variability in thermal response.
Grain boundaries and other defects act as stress concentrators and potential hosts for short-range compositional segregation.
Elevated temperature produces preferential atomic mobility at grain boundaries.
Structural disorder and possible segregation at grain boundaries lower their local melting points.
Liquid pockets nucleate at grain boundaries and subsequently grow and merge, causing the solid-to-liquid transition.
Localized premelting at grain boundaries precedes uniform nanoparticle melting.
Grain-boundary premelting produces discrete endothermic events detectable by differential scanning calorimetry.
In situ TEM can reveal liquid-phase formation at defect sites before bulk melting.
Rapid heating or substantial compositional heterogeneity could alter the melting pathway.
